title: 大图加载策略：Region Decode、Tile 与峰值控制
key_conclusions: Large image viewers should decode by viewport and zoom level instead of decoding the full source image.
Tile size, visible tile count, prefetch radius, active zoom levels, and eviction policy define the memory budget.
CPU pixel cache and GPU/Graphics upload must be measured separately because a tile can cost memory in both places.
Peak validation requires pan/zoom workloads, before/after meminfo, showmap/smaps, Graphics evidence, and cache plateau checks.
shallow_points: The article does not include a real large-image viewer sample or meminfo timeline.
It does not validate BitmapRegionDecoder behavior across formats, Android versions, and hardware bitmap paths.
It does not include measured tile size, prefetch, and zoom-level tradeoff data.
It does not compare third-party subsampling image viewers.
discovered_connections: Day 44's Glide cache, pool, and lifecycle boundaries become tile cache and decode task boundaries for large images.
Day 43's sampling and transform peak controls apply to each tile and zoom level.
Day 42's Native Heap versus Graphics attribution is needed because tiles can exist in CPU pixels and GPU resources.
Day 46 should deepen the Graphics, RenderThread, GPU upload, and dma-buf parts of this path.
